title: Fairfax County homebuilder convicted of defrauding clients - NewsBreak
text:
By Makea Luzader No media credit provided. ,
5 hours ago
FAIRFAX COUNTY, Va. ( DC News Now ) — Fairfax County Commonwealth’s Attorney Steve Descano announced Wednesday that a homebuilder was convicted of defrauding clients between 2021 and 2023.
According to a release from Descano’s office, Richard Craig Tadlock contracted with six families in Fairfax to build custom homes for them in 2021 and 2022. Despite promises, work was never finished on any of the houses.
Descano said that some homes never moved past the initial construction stages.
According to the Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office, Tadlock received around $1.2 million for work that he never completed.
Final defendant sentenced in $31 million coupon fraud scheme Prosecutors claimed that Tadlock intended to defraud clients as soon as contracts were signed. Evidence showed that he never bought many of the supplies that had been paid for, and that he did not give progress updates to families.
“The defendant knowingly took money from multiple victims, even when he never intended to do the necessary construction work on their homes. His pattern of avoiding engagement kept six families in limbo for years, tying up some victims’ life savings in projects that were going nowhere,” Descano said in a statement.
Tadlock faces up to 120 years in prison. His sentencing is scheduled for Sept. 10.
